messages.author: 4b58dae6963fae5e
messages.subject: Power parameter?
parts:
My lab mate and I are trying to figure out what the "power parameter" is on the Parameter Estimates tab of the Results log. The manual doesn't discuss it and we haven't found any helpful resources online. What does it mean? What impacts it? And what is considered acceptable? 

***
Detection Fct/Global/Parameter Estimates

Effort: XXXX
# samples: XXX
Width: XXX
Left: XXX
# observations: XX

Model
   Hazard Rate Key, k(y) = 1 - Exp (-(y/s)**-A(2))

  s = A(1) * Exp (fcn(A(3)) + fcn(A(4)) + ...
  Parameter A(1) is the intercept of the scale parameter s.
  Parameter A(2) is the power parameter.
  Parameter A(3) is the coefficient of level -0.40 of factor covariate....

***

Happy to post any more info if necessary, just tedious working across a few computers from home.

Thank you!

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Power parameter?
parts:
Brandon

The output you show is for the fit of a hazard rate key function with a covariate perhaps.  The covariate isn't related to your question.  The hazard rate key function is a two parameter model with a shape and equation shown below:

This figure is taken from our online lecture materials, Slide 10 of this PDF

The figure shows the effect of beta upon the shape of the detection function; the larger the value of beta, the more sharply the detection function declines beyond the shoulder.

https://workshops.distancesampling.org/online-course/lecturepdfs/Ch1/L1-4%20Choosing%20a%20Detection%20Function.pdf

The parameter labelled "power" in the Distance for Windows output is the same as the Greek symbol  β.


BEwdddsadfadf

dd\beta

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Power parameter?
parts:
Brandon

Don't know there is a value of beta that would trigger a red flag.  The plotted detection function would serve as a guide.  As you suggest, large values of beta estimates suggest detectability falls precipitously at some value.  You'd likely want to consult with those who collected the data to assess the plausibility of the estimated detection function.

Thanks, Eric! This helps a lot. Are there any values for β that might reflect a problem with the data? I can could see that if it's too high you effectively have a wall limiting your effective sighting distance. Not sure if that's just a potential reality that would be worth discussing in the results or if it suggests some mathematical/sampling issue.
